registry_info.name: arguments
registry_info.description: A hall's argument stood on its floor: the authored cardboard thinking of commons/data/arguments/<hall>.json (plates, stickers, threads round a hero artifact) and the visual arguments built for it from the tower's prefabs.
registry_info.theoretical_grounding: An explanation is somebody's: these are written in the first person, say where the writer does not know, and keep the hall text's own words apart from the writer's.

argument_floor.name: An Argument, Stood on a Floor
argument_floor.description: A hall's authored argument standing in the tower: each plate a sheet of cardboard propped on two crates with its notes in marker (front) and in pink (back), its stickers along the bottom (yellow: a claim, red: what it is not, blue: an open question, white: the hall text word for word), a pole behind each plate and red threads between the poles, each with its word on a tag; a ring of tape and two work lights for the hero artifact. Reads commons/data/arguments/<hall>.json and letters it in the handwriting fonts. A stand-in until the sticker app's cardboard constructions land in VR: nothing here can be edited by a visitor. Axis hall: which hall's argument.
argument_floor.qfep_connection: Making sense is somebody's work and leaves its wrong turns visible: the plates keep what was blamed first beside what held.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Two halls' arguments are about ten cardboard plates each (1.34 x 1.8 m) at different places and turns across a floor of 42 x 18 m, with different threads between them. Seen from the bench's standpoint a plate is a sliver of about 1 square metre; some twenty plates that do not coincide and some thirty-five threads of a centimetre's width differ, of a floor that fills about half the frame: 20 / 756 x 0.5 = 1.3 % from the plates alone as a flat rasteriser sees them; lettering, stickers and the work lights' pools add to it in a real render, so 4 % is what I expect and 1.3 % is the floor.

diagonal_grid.name: The Grid and the Row That Is Not on It
diagonal_grid.description: A visual argument for the Russell hall: the workbench's own four sets as a floor grid of timber panels - rows the things, columns the same things, a blue ball where the row contains the column, the diagonal in pink frames (does a thing contain itself: four times no). South of it, outside, a plank with the opposite of the diagonal at every place. Standing on a diagonal place, the board says where the new row disagrees with that row: it is not on the list. Standing still on EVERYTHING declares the list complete: the row is carried in as a fifth row with a column of its own, and its own place must hold a ball exactly when it does not - nothing is put there, and nothing blinks. Axis stage: grid, new_row, everything.
diagonal_grid.qfep_connection: The row is harmless outside the list. The trouble is the claim that the list was everything.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: grid and new_row differ by the plank (4 x 0.25 m), its four yellow balls (0.1 square metres each) and one line of floor words: about 1.6 square metres of a scene of 30 that fills about half the frame: 2.7 %; a flat rasteriser sees the low plank and small balls poorly, so 1.2 % as the floor. everything differs from both by nine more panels.

checking_station.name: The Checking Station
checking_station.description: A visual argument in the form of a robot station, for the Goedel hall: three ways a search stops, and finding is not checking. A robot of a construction cube on trace balls brings candidates to a gate of crates and a timber panel. Each candidate is a derivation in the hall's own toy syntax (axiom 0, rule w -> Sw), one step longer than the last, every fourth with a middle line lost; the gate checks it against what was asked with the bench's own checker (foundations-lineage/derivation.gd: verify) and passes it through or has it pushed aside. The station counts what it checked and never says 'none will pass'. Axis asks: SSS0 (the fourth candidate passes), SSSSSSSS0 (eight refusals, then the ninth: slow, not impossible), 0S (nothing the rule makes ends in an S: impossible, and the station looks exactly as it does while it is being slow - the reason is an argument on the board, not a check at the gate). Three plates ask. The motion is kinematic.
checking_station.qfep_connection: A machine that only refuses cannot tell you whether it is being slow or facing the impossible. That difference is made by an argument, from outside.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: At rest, before a candidate has been checked, the three stations are the same station: the same row, gate and robot. They differ by the words on the gate's screen ('asked for ...', about 0.3 x 0.2 m of lettering) and one line of the board. That is the point of the work - slow and impossible look alike from outside - and it means a still cannot tell them apart: about 0.06 square metres of 25 that fill half the frame, 0.1 %; with the board's line, 0.3 %. The sweep will say INERT; the difference is in what happens after eight candidates, which a still does not hold.

walked_triangle.name: The Walked Triangle
walked_triangle.description: A visual argument in the form of a playground, for the non-Euclidean hall: what counts as straight. A walkable dome - the cap of a sphere six metres in radius, 6.4 m across and 0.9 m high - with two cones as corners A and B; the body stepping onto it is corner C. The sides are drawn on the surface as the straightest paths that stay on it, the board gives the three angles and their sum, more than 180 and growing with the triangle. A plank through the dome from cone to cone is the shorter way that has left the space. North of the dome the same three coordinate pairs are read as a plane on a mat: 180, wherever the body stands. The model is the tutorial's own (noneuclid-lineage/surface_triangle.gd: corner, edge, measure), read once as sphere and once as plane. Axis reading: both, sphere, plane.
walked_triangle.qfep_connection: The record of three pairs travels between the plane and the dome; the angles do not. What counts as straight is a decision about the space the corners belong to.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: both and sphere differ by the mat north of the dome: a dark sheet 3.4 x 3.0 m with three balls, three tapes and a line of words - about 10 square metres of a scene of 80 that fills about half the frame: 6 %; the mat is dark and flat against a grey floor, so a flat rasteriser sees mostly its outline: 2 % as the floor. plane removes the dome (32 square metres of pale cap) and differs from both by far more.

standing_word.name: A Word Standing on the Floor
standing_word.description: One word in thick red letters, as tall as a person, standing on the slab: a landmark for a hall's idea. From the front it reads; from behind it is the same letters the wrong way round. Solid: a body walks round it. Axis word: ERROR, NULL, INFINITY, TRUE, PROVABLE, EVERYTHING - the words the foundations halls keep coming back to; text, when not empty, stands instead. tall is the height of a capital in metres, deep the extrusion, fit_width the most room along the floor (a longer word is made smaller, not cut). A TextMesh in commons/font/static/Roboto_Condensed-ExtraBold.ttf (Roboto-Black cannot be used: its P and R do not triangulate).
standing_word.qfep_connection: A word has a side it is said from: read from behind, the same letters are the wrong way round and nobody arranged it.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Two words of the same red letters at the same height share a letter shape here and there (ERROR and TRUE share R, U-less; E at different places) but no letter stands in the same place, so most of the lettered area differs: letters cover about a third of the frame from the bench's standpoint and two different words overlap in perhaps half of their strokes: 0.33 x 0.5 = 16 %; a flat rasteriser sees the faces without the extrusion's sides, so 6 % as the floor.

meeting_point.name: Where Do They Meet?
meeting_point.description: A visual argument in the form of a playground, for the Euclid hall: the fifth postulate at the size of the floor. A first line on text tape the length of the slab; a point P a metre and a half off it; the gold line through P with no shortfall; four lines through P that fall 20, 10, 5 and 3 degrees short of two right angles, each with a cone where it meets the first line (4, 9, 17 and 29 m along). A body in the lane between the lines carries a pink line from P and a stake where that line meets the first: at the body's feet on the first line, running away east as the body steps toward the gold line, off the edge of the building. On the gold line the reading is withheld (the instrument's threshold, 0.05 degrees, and it says so); beyond it the meeting is behind P. Nothing shows that the gold line never meets: it is accepted, not walked. Axis shortfall: where the pink line rests - wide (8 degrees), narrow (2.5), none. The row stands at x 0 of its floor, facing 0.
meeting_point.qfep_connection: An assumption held so long it reads like a result: every line but one has a meeting that can be walked to, and the one that has none is the one that was asked for like a favour.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The work is 41 m long and 3 m deep: a thin band. narrow and none differ by a pink line 4 cm wide swung 2.5 degrees over 34 m (1.4 square metres laid, 1.4 lifted) and by the stake (a pole 1.7 m high with a ball and a tag, about 0.3 square metres seen from the side): 3.1 square metres of a band of 123 that fills perhaps 8 % of the frame: 0.2 %. This axis is made to be walked, not photographed whole; I expect the critic to call it small from the bench's standpoint and predict so.

cornered_block.name: Three Corners and You Are Home
cornered_block.description: A playable non-Euclidean space for the non-Euclidean hall: a square block with a closed corridor round it and one door. Keep the block on your left and count the corners, each a right angle drawn on the floor: after three you stand at the door again - a closed walk of 270 degrees on a floor that is flat under every step. The 90 too many sit at one point inside the block, as at the corner of a cube. The inside has three quarter-sectors where the building has four: the four sides are built alike, the numbers and the door are lettered from where the body stands, and when the body turns onto a side the glued space does not have it is turned about the block's middle by a quarter in the same frame. Axis corners: three, four (an ordinary block), five (450 degrees: the disk's surplus at one point). Not tried in a headset.
cornered_block.qfep_connection: The floor is ordinary under every step and the walk still closes after three right angles: what a space is cannot be read off any one piece of it.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: From outside the three are one closed cardboard block; what differs is the sign on the door's screen (one numeral, 25 cm high) and the words on the board (about 3.4 x 1.5 m, mostly the same lines). Changed lettering covers perhaps a tenth of the board: 0.5 square metres of a scene of about 60 that fills half the frame: 0.4 %; a flat rasteriser reads lettering poorly: 0.3 %. The axis lives inside, in what a walk does; a still of the outside will call it decoration and I predict so.

mirror_lap.name: One Lap and Your Left Is Your Right
mirror_lap.description: A playable non-Euclidean space for the non-Euclidean hall: a corridor joined to itself the other way up - a Moebius band laid on a floor. Go in: the word LEFT stands on your left. Walk a lap of left turns and come to it again: it stands on your right and reads backwards, every corner now turns right, and the door stays shut, because outside nothing is mirrored. A second lap puts everything back. Nothing is bent and every triangle keeps 180 degrees. Built as it must be for a body that cannot be mirrored: two blocks either side of one shared stretch; lap one goes round the north block, lap two round the south block, its mirror image; the shared stretch's word, skirtings, door lettering and end openings are turned over while a block hides them. The body is never moved. Axis lap: first, second (which sheet the door opens onto).
mirror_lap.qfep_connection: Left and right are not properties of a body or of a place but of a way round a space; one lap and the word for your hand is on the other hand, and nothing says which of you turned.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The two differ only inside, under a roof: the word and the skirtings change walls and two openings change places. From any standpoint outside, the block is the same closed cardboard box with the same door and the same board: 0 %. That is a fact about standing outside a roof, not about the axis; from the door, looking in, the red word alone is about 2.2 x 0.55 m and moves 1.1 m.

walked_tiling.name: Five Squares at Every Corner
walked_tiling.description: A playable non-Euclidean space for the non-Euclidean hall: a round deck, 5.2 m across, that shows under and round the one who walks it a floor of square tiles of which five meet at every corner - the disk's geometry under the feet. True to size where you stand, squeezed toward a rim that keeps three metres from you. A pink square, 1.4 m a side, is painted on the deck itself. Stand still on START: the tile under you turns red, home, with an arrow pointing north. Walk the square back to START: on the slab the walk closes, on this floor home is 2.4 m away and its arrow has turned 159 degrees; a pointer at your feet shows where it went. Axis corner: five, four (a flat floor: the tiles stay put and the walk closes), three (a cube's skin, rounded: six tiles in all; home 1.2 m away, turned the other way). The body is never moved: its steps are composed as motions of the floor and the deck's shader draws the tiling from them.
walked_tiling.qfep_connection: The same four turns and the same paces: whether you are home afterwards is not a fact about the walk but about the floor it was made on.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The deck is a disk of 21 square metres; its tiles' dark lines (4 cm wide, about 3.5 m of edge to a square metre of floor) cover about a seventh of it in either tiling, and the two grids coincide only near START, so most line pixels differ: about 5 square metres of changed deck. The deck fills perhaps a third of the frame from the bench's standpoint: 5 / 21 x 0.33 = 8 %; lines seen at a low angle thin out, so 4 %. The floor of this prediction is not a rasteriser's - a flat rasteriser cannot run the deck's shader and sees one plain disk: 0 %.

endless_stair.name: A Stair That Only Goes Up and Comes Back
endless_stair.description: A visual argument in the form of a playground, for the Escher hall: the staircase that goes up on all four sides and comes back to where it started, at body size. A square stairwell round a block, 5 m square and 4.9 m high, its door a flight above the floor at the top of a ramp. Keep the block on your left and climb: every flight rises 0.6 m, and after four you are at the door again. It keeps the other agreement the hall names, a moved room: what stands is one honest lap; the body lives on two of its flights, and at the corner where it would step onto the third it is set down 1.2 m and turned half about onto the first, a place built to look exactly like the one it left, while the numbers on the block are lettered from where it stands. The wall inside keeps count: metres climbed, metres above the door, metres taken back. Axis agreement: moved, kept (one up all the way round: the four rising flights cannot close and the stair ends 1.8 m above its door). Not tried in a headset.
endless_stair.qfep_connection: Every flight is honest and every corner is honest; what cannot be had is all of them at once under one up. The stair closes by changing the agreement, and keeps the receipt on its wall.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: From outside the two are one closed cardboard stairwell with the same ramp and door; only the board's words differ (3.4 x 1.5 m, about half its lines): perhaps 1 square metre of lettering changed in a scene of 70 that fills half the frame: 0.7 %; lettering reads poorly at this size: 0.3 %. The axis is what a climb does; a still of the outside will call it decoration and I predict so.

small_planet.name: A Small Planet
small_planet.description: A non-Euclidean biome: a world ten metres across with grass, flowers, stones, trees, mushrooms and five beetles on it, no edge and no end. A door on the floor leads onto it. Walk straight for 31.4 m and the door you came by rises over the horizon in front of you; the beetles walk straight too and every two of their lines cross twice - there are no parallels; a quarter round, left, a quarter, left, a quarter brings you to the door after three right angles, and the door has turned by a quarter. The planet hangs 160 m north of the tower, a ball seen from the floor; the door moves the body there. On the planet the body is not moved again: the ground under its feet is flat and still, and the planet, what grows on it and its own sky of stars are turned under the body by exactly its steps. Axis across: six, ten, twenty metres. Not tried in a headset.
small_planet.qfep_connection: A world can be finite and have no edge: walking straight is how you come home, and what lives there walks lines that all meet.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: On a bench (no tower) the planet stands behind its door. A ball 6 m across beside one 10 m across: seen from the bench's standpoint the larger fills about 2.8 times the area of the smaller, and the frame is fitted to the larger subject each time, so the door shrinks instead: the door and board (about 8 square metres of facing) change scale by 10/6 and the ball's grass pattern is laid afresh. Most of the subject's pixels differ: I expect well over 12 %; 12 % is the floor (ball outlines alone).

roof_stair.name: The Roof Where Everyone Climbs
roof_stair.description: The stair that only goes up and comes back, in the open and drawn like a print: a door on the floor leads to a roof where wide steps, 2.2 m across, climb round a tower past a pavilion on every corner. No light, a tone for each way a face looks, engraved lines; robed walkers trudge up along the tower and others down along the parapet, and small figures walk on the tower's walls as if the walls were floors. Every flight goes up; after four you are in the door's pavilion again. One honest lap stands; the body lives on two of its flights and is set down 1.2 m and turned half about at the corner where it would step onto the third - unseen in the open because everything in view is the same after a half turn and a drop of 1.2 m: the tower repeats on four sides and every 1.2 m, the clouds come in opposite pairs, every walker is placed from where the body stands. Tablets on the tower count metres climbed, above the door and taken back. The roof hangs 160 m south of the tower in a sky of its own. Axis walkers: both, up, none. An original place in the manner of an impossible print. Not tried in a headset.
roof_stair.qfep_connection: For the stair to close unseen, the whole world round it had to be made the same from two places: an impossible object is paid for by the uniformity of everything else.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: On a bench the roof stands behind its door. both and up differ by the pale walkers coming down: five figures, of which three or four are on the three sides in view; each about 1.4 x 0.6 m seen from the side, 0.8 square metres: 3 square metres of a subject (tower 3.2 m wide and tall, stair 7.6 m across) of about 150 that fills most of the frame: 2 %; pale robes against pale stone change tone, not outline: 0.6 %. none removes the seven dark ones too and differs by far more.

made_walk.name: Only What You Have Made
made_walk.description: A visual argument in the form of a playground, for the Brouwer hall: the choice sequence as a walkway out over the edge of the slab. A deck at the edge and beyond it nothing. Stand still on 0 or on 1 and one plank is laid ahead, to the left for 0, to the right for 1, with its bead and its value; walk out onto it; wait, and nothing comes. The walkway is the row: 0, 1 and 1, 0 are different shapes under the feet. The board answers the finite question (does your row hold a 1? yes, plank 3: a witness is an address you can stand on) and leaves the other open (will a 1 ever come? your zeros do not say). Sixteen planks fill the instrument, not the row. Axis author: hand (it waits), clock (a rule lays 0, 1, 0, 1 every two seconds whoever is there and takes the planks up again when it is full). Stands at a slab edge, facing 0; a body that steps off is brought back by the tower.
made_walk.qfep_connection: What is underfoot is exactly what was chosen; ahead there is no floor waiting to be revealed. And the two plates were there before the foot: the freedom had a shape.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: At the moment a still is taken hand has no planks (nobody chose) and clock has laid some: after the bench's settle of a third of a second, none; after two seconds, one. So the two stills differ by the two plates (0.45 square metres, shown only by hand), the board's words, and at most one plank of 1.5 square metres: about 2.5 square metres of a scene of 12 that fills a third of the frame: 7 %; if the still falls before the first plank, 2 %. I predict the lower number and say why: the clock's row is a thing in time.

consequence_yard.name: What Follows?
consequence_yard.description: A visual argument in the form of a playground, for the Florensky hall: explosion and its refusal, as doors. Seven doors in a row, a sentence over each: P (the door is open), not-P, P and not-P, P or not-P, P or the alarm rang, Q (the alarm rang), not-Q. Stand still on a plate to give or take back a report, P or not-P; every door whose sentence follows swings open and can be walked through. Behind Q hangs a bell. Under the four-valued rule of the hall's working copy (told true, told false, both, neither) both reports can be held and five doors open, the bell's stays shut: no support; with no reports nothing opens, not even P or not-P. A third plate reads the same reports classically: with both, nothing can fit them, so nothing can fail - all seven open and the visitor can go in and ring an alarm nobody reported. Axis rule: four, classical.
consequence_yard.qfep_connection: Keeping two reports that disagree costs two places in memory. What it licenses is a rule somebody chose - and the rule is what lets a body through.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: With no reports (the state a still is taken in) four opens nothing and classical opens one door, 'P or not-P': one leaf of 0.95 x 2.15 m swung away from its opening, uncovering a dark bay: about 2 square metres changed of a front of 8.9 x 2.6 = 23 that fills about a third of the frame: 3 %; the leaf is pale against a pale wall behind: 1.5 %. The board's two changed lines are below what a still resolves.

six_cards.name: A Sentence, Its Scope, Its Evidence
six_cards.description: A visual argument in the form of a robot station, for the Crisis Synthesis hall: the hall's six cards at body size. Six cardboard cards on crates, each with a sentence in large letters, its scope, its evidence and a record. Stand still on the mark before a card and its check is run there and then, and the record is written with what it does not show: a failed membership case (the diagonal row against four sets), a search to a budget (the Goedel hall's own checker; 4 stops short, 8 finds it), a measured return (four heights, the differences summed round), an exhibited witness (a row of eight looked through for a 1), a countermodel (both reports held, the alarm under the four-valued tables). The sixth card carries a claim from the cardboard on these floors, written by the AI that wrote this description, with no procedure attached: its mark runs nothing and says so. Axis sixth: large (its letters as large as the checked ones, as the hall asks), small.
six_cards.qfep_connection: Five warrants and no common certificate; and one sentence by the writer of all this, as large as the rest, with nothing behind it. Size is not evidence, and the card says who it is.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The two differ by the lettering of one sentence on one card of six: three lines of 5 cm letters against 2.4 cm ones, on a patch of about 1.3 x 0.4 m: half a square metre of thin strokes in a row of cards 8.8 m wide and 2.2 m high that fills about a third of the frame: 0.9 % of the subject, a third of it ink: 0.4 %. The axis is true to its subject: the hall's point is that this difference is small and is not evidence.

halving_door.name: Every Door, Half as Far
halving_door.description: A playable space for the non-Euclidean hall: the disk's rule for distance, walked along one line. A plank goes out over the slab's edge to a cardboard funnel six metres long; through its mouth a door is seen, and behind it a door half the size, half as far from the tip, and so on. Inside, every door is as far as the last was (4.2 m of walking) and as large when reached, and the tip stays six metres ahead: there is no last door. The visitor is not made smaller: the funnel is made larger round the visitor, about its own tip, by exactly the visitor's steps (scale e^(metres/6)), the door behind papered over. The body is not moved, except sideways on the way out by however far the walls pushed it off the plank's line. A flag on the funnel's back marks how far the last visitor got. Axis ratio: half, two_thirds, three_quarters - any ratio under one gives a rim that is never reached. Benched in tools/probes/halving_door_bench.py. Not tried in a headset.
halving_door.qfep_connection: A boundary that can be drawn and pointed at, and that no walk arrives at: the distance belongs to the rule for a step, not to the picture.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: From outside the funnel is the same card pyramid at every ratio (two sides of 7.8 m2 and a back of 9.6 m2: about 25 m2). What differs: the lines where the doors come through the card (each 2 cm wide and 3.2 q^k long: 9.6 m of line against 12.8 m, 0.06 m2 apart) and what is seen through the mouth (1.1 x 2.1 m: the first inner door at 4 m from the tip, two thirds the size, against 4.5 m and three quarters; perhaps a fifth of that opening changes: 0.46 m2). 0.52 of 25: 2 %. The plank, rails and board do not change.

total_line.name: One Number Is a Line on This Floor
total_line.description: A playground for the QFEP introduction hall: the console's question - can two different arrangements give the same number? - at body size. A painted floor six metres square: a step east is F, a step north is E, and the floor is banded by the console's own total, F - lambda E + 0.3 phi. Stand still and the floor keeps that place: a flag, and a red line through every other place with the same total. Walk the line: the large number on the stand does not move, and the four-axis shape beside it does - the pale outline remembers what the total cannot. Plates beside the floor set lambda (0, a half, 1) and phi (0, 1): with lambda at zero the lines run north and a walk in E changes nothing; with phi raised the kept number is found somewhere else. It measures nothing; it is the hall's arithmetic laid out. Axis weight: zero, half, one - the lambda the floor starts with.
total_line.qfep_connection: One number can summarise several contributions while concealing how they compensated for one another: here the concealment has a shape, a line, and a body can stand at both ends of it.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The floor is 36 m2 of bands a tenth of the total wide. At weight half the bands are 0.54 m wide and lean 27 degrees from north; at one they are 0.42 m wide and lean 45. Two sets of stripes of about that width at 18 degrees to each other disagree over roughly half the floor, but neighbouring bands differ only by a tenth of the ramp and a 8 % tone step, so about a fifth of the disagreeing area reads as a different colour: 36 x 0.5 x 0.2 = 3.6 m2, of a subject (floor, stand, plates, board) of about 40 m2: 9 %. The stand's shape changes one vertex (lambda 0.5 to 1 on a 0.75 m axis): under 0.3 m2. Zero against half is further apart: the lines stand upright.

guessing_walk.name: Whose Expectation Meets It?
guessing_walk.description: A playground for the QFEP F-term hall: its prediction study with a body for a predictor. Twelve bits lie under card in two lanes: the south lane is EXPECT 0, the north lane EXPECT 1. A stand shows forty-eight bits the source gave before. Walk: each row is uncovered as it is stepped into, and an amber bar marks a bit that refused the guess. AGAIN covers the same twelve bits: walked in the other lane the row has not changed and the misses have. Plates set the source (p 0.1, 0.5, 0.9): 0.1 and 0.9 are equally uncertain and ask for opposite lanes. One plate does what the hall warns of, CHANGE THE WORLD INSTEAD: every bit that refused the walker is rewritten to where the walker stood and stamped; no misses, and the stand says the row is no longer a sample of its source. The row is the first twelve of the hall workbench's own stored draws. Axis source: tenth, half, nine_tenths.
guessing_walk.qfep_connection: When a world is called difficult, whose expectation is meeting it? The expectation can be changed with a step; the plate at the end changes the world instead, and says what that costs.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: At rest the twelve rows are under card at every source, so the row itself does not change. What does: the stand's forty-eight evidence cells (0.14 m square: from half to nine tenths about 19 of them turn from dark to cyan, 0.37 m2), two plates trade their highlight (2 x 0.7 m2), and two lines of figures. 1.8 m2 of a subject of about 40 m2 (row 24, stand 8, plates 3.5, board 5): 4 %. Tenth against nine tenths is further: about 38 cells.

drawn_tree.name: Who Drew the Tree?
drawn_tree.description: A playground for the QFEP E-term hall: the fan's tree, to be the traveller in. Sixteen endings from four forks of two, taped on the floor from START. A walked path lights, and a bead is hung at the ending reached. A stand gives the entropy twice: counted, as if every ending were equally likely (ln 16), and as walked, from where travellers arrived. PRUNE A and PRUNE B each close four amber gates and leave eight endings: the same count and entropy, different endings; what lay beyond a gate is no longer drawn, and beads that hung there are lost. OPEN returns the endings, not the beads, and the stand says how many were lost. And what the fan cannot do: stand still at one of the eight last forks and a third way is drawn to an ending nobody specified - only at the last forks, where room was left, and the board says so. Axis drawn: open, pruned_a, pruned_b.
drawn_tree.qfep_connection: A count of endings says neither which endings nor who arrives at them, and a reopened route does not return what was lost when it closed. Who drew the tree, and where may another branch be asked for?

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Both close four gates and take eight endings off the floor; they differ in WHICH. Each state shows four amber gates (0.9 x 1.0 m frames of 6 cm bar: about 0.15 m2 of bar each) and four small subtrees (a fork plate, two ending plates, two tapes, two rods: about 0.5 m2 each) that the other does not: 2 x 4 x 0.65 = 5.2 m2 exchanged, but thin: tapes and bars cover perhaps a quarter of that: 1.3 m2 of a subject (tree 10 x 6 m of sparse marks, stand 7, plates 2, board 5: about 40 m2 seen): 3 %. One plate's highlight moves. The stand prints the same count and the same entropy for both, which is the point.

worn_path.name: The Light Recommends, the Feet Decide
worn_path.description: A playground for the QFEP lambda hall: a recommendation, an arrangement and a record of use, kept apart. A field six metres by ten of card tiles that darken where feet have gone. Three rows of posts cross it, each with one gap, and the gaps line up. A lit strip runs the length of the field: at first through the gaps. Plates move the light west or east, where it points at posts; the feet still go through the gaps, and the worn path says so. A stand counts crossings, the share of steps taken on the lit strip, where the field is most worn and how far the light lies from that. One plate lights what was worn: the recommendation follows use. Another sweeps the field. It records where feet went and no reason. Axis lit: gap, west, east - where the light lies when the field is found.
worn_path.qfep_connection: Which available alternatives are made inviting, and by what: a light that can be moved, or an arrangement that cannot? And when the next visitor sees where the first one walked, whose decision is theirs?

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The field, posts, plates, stand and board are the same at every value. What moves is the lit strip, one metre wide and ten long (10 m2 of a subject of about 85 m2: field 60, stand 9, plates 4, board 5, approach). From gap (1.25 m west of the middle) to west (2.25 m west) the strip shifts by its own width, so about 10 m2 of floor changes between lit and unlit and 10 m2 the other way, but the strip is a pale wash over pale card, perhaps a quarter of full contrast: 20 x 0.25 = 5 m2 of 85: 6 %. One plate's highlight moves and one line on the stand. Gap against east is no further in area but crosses the posts.

signed_walk.name: A Weight, a Change, a Product
signed_walk.description: A playground for the QFEP phi hall: its three separate quantities, with a body for the changing one. A track five metres long: where the visitor stands on it is a reading from 0 to 1, and it is looked at once a second. A stand keeps three numbers apart: the weight phi (plates: -1, 0, +1; it starts at 0), the change since the last look, and their product, with an arrow up or down. A positive weight and a falling reading give a negative product; negative times negative is positive, and the stand says the arithmetic does not say whether that is good. The last looks stay on the track as dots, so that a slow walk and a fast one over the same stretch can be told apart; SNAPSHOT keeps only the latest, and then there is no change to show. EARLIER LABELS puts RESIST and EMBRACE over the two signs, and nothing else changes. Axis labels: hidden, shown.
signed_walk.qfep_connection: Change can have a direction without that direction meaning improvement: a weight, a change and their product are three numbers, and a word hung over a sign is a fourth thing that the arithmetic never contained.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The only difference is two words, RESIST and EMBRACE, standing over the two sign plates: letters 0.28 m tall, about 1.5 m and 1.7 m long, on a subject of track, stand, five plates and board of about 30 m2 seen. Two strips of 0.45 m2 of which lettering covers perhaps half: 0.45 m2 of 30: 1.5 %. That is small on purpose: the hall's own point is that nothing else changes when the words appear. One plate's highlight changes too.

step_spiral.name: The Same Rule in Larger Steps
step_spiral.description: A playground for the QFEP edge-of-chaos hall: which changes belong to the model, and which to the way its calculation is run. One rule - go round the pole at one rate, a circle - computed a step at a time from the same start for the same model time (one turn), in two step sizes side by side: stones and tape on the floor, amber for the coarse steps and cyan for the fine. Every step leaves the circle a little, so each computation ends outside it, the coarse one further: a spiral the step size made. A stand gives the two ends and the difference between them. A plate halves both step sizes; one adds a wall that clips whatever passes it, as an earlier version of the hall's screen did: then the two ends agree and both are wrong, and the coarse path is a ring the wall made. A ball runs the coarse path; RUN FASTER moves it three times as fast along the same stones. Benched in tools/probes/step_spiral_bench.py. Axis pair: coarse, fine.
step_spiral.qfep_connection: A pattern can be made by the rule or by the way the rule is run; agreement between two step sizes is a reason for trust, and a number that reports agreement can improve while nothing becomes truer.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Both values draw the rule's circle, the pole, the stand, the plates and the board alike, and both draw the 48-step path (amber at fine, cyan at coarse: the same stones in another colour). What differs: coarse adds the 24-step path, a spiral of 24 tapes ending 3.55 m out (about 17 m of tape 6 cm wide: 1.0 m2, and 25 stones); fine adds the 96-step path instead (about 11 m of tape: 0.7 m2, 97 small stones). So roughly 1.7 m2 of marks exchanged and 0.9 m2 recoloured on a subject of about 50 m2 (a 7.6 m disc of floor seen, stand 9, plates 4, board 5): 5 %.

offered_used.name: What the Hand Offers, What the Body Uses
offered_used.description: A playground for the QFEP sandbox hall: its wiring study with a receiver a body can test with itself. A rail five metres long: where the visitor last walked along it is the value offered, and a puck stays there. North of it a gate of two sliding panels stands open by the value it uses. A strip between them is the route: at first cut. Walk the rail: the puck follows, the gate does not. CONNECT / CUT makes the route and the gate takes what the rail offers; open it and walk through. Close it, cut the route and walk the rail back: the gate stays shut, having kept the last value it was given. OTHER MAPPING turns the consequence round: the same number closes what it opened, and the stand says someone wrote both. A second gate beside it moves by itself; no route leads to it. The stand always shows both sides: offered at the rail, used at the gate. Axis route: cut, connected.
offered_used.qfep_connection: A control changes a system only where a route carries it and a mapping uses it; cutting the route leaves the last decision in force; and the consequence of a number was written by someone.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Found cut, the gate uses 0.10 and stands 0.24 m open; found connected it uses the offered 0.50 and stands 1.20 m open: each of its two panels (1.2 x 2.2 m) stands 0.48 m further out, uncovering 2 x 0.48 x 2.2 = 2.1 m2 of what lies behind and covering as much. The route strip (0.14 x 1.75 m) turns from grey to cyan: 0.25 m2. Three lines of the stand change. About 2.4 m2 of a subject of some 60 m2 (two gates 23, rail 6, stand 7, plates, board, floor between): 4 %. The neighbour gate differs by its own clock, not by the axis.

asked_read_measured.name: Asked, Read Back, Measured
asked_read_measured.description: A robot station for the QFEP synthesis hall: its three things to check against one another, on a body tall enough to watch. A mast three metres tall on a sprung foot; PULSE strikes it and it sways. A stand has three columns for each of three properties: what a plate asked for, what the property reads back, and what was measured from the mast's own motion (the time of a swing, and how much of a swing is left after one more); under them the tip's place over the last twelve seconds. Damping is taken at once. Stiffness is read back at once and does nothing until REBUILD: the rings on the foot are the spring as built. Drag is asked, read back and used by nothing. BREATHE / STEADY gives or stops a slow imposed sway; steady, the mast goes on moving, and the stand says steady is not still. Axis built: soft, middle, stiff.
asked_read_measured.qfep_connection: What was requested, what a property reports and what a body does are three accounts; only the third is the body's, and it needs a trace kept over time.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: At rest the mast stands upright at every value. What differs is the spring on its foot: six rings against nine (three more rings, each a torus 0.32 m across and 0.06 thick: about 0.02 m2 seen each, 0.06 m2), and two figures on the stand (9 against 16, twice). On a subject of some 30 m2 (stand 13, mast, plates 5, board 5, floor between): 0.06 + 0.1 of lettering: under 1 %. The axis is honest and small in a still: what it changes is the time of a swing, which a still cannot hold. Soft against stiff is twice that.

room_to_tell_apart.name: Room To Tell Apart
room_to_tell_apart.description: A playground for the algorithmic bias hall: its table of words at the size of a body. Twenty-four posts in two fields of twelve, a warm or grey band and a number on each, no word. A rail: walk along it and the warm twelve are pressed toward one place, to a fifth of their spread, while the grey twelve spread. A stand counts three things for each colour: how many are present (always twelve), how many have room round them (a body's width to the nearest other post), and how many are hidden behind another from where the visitor stands. The rail changes the second, the visitor's feet the third, nothing the first. Open, a body walks between the warm posts; pressed, they are one thing to walk round. Standing still between two warm posts keeps that pair where it was when the rest are pressed. OTHER GROUPING makes another twelve warm. Axis pressed: open, half, pressed.
room_to_tell_apart.qfep_connection: Being present in a representation and having room in it to be told apart are two counts; a control changes the second while the first stays full, and the grouping it acts on was chosen by someone.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Twenty-four posts, each 0.14 m wide and 1.3 m tall with a number above: about 0.25 m2 seen each. Between half and pressed the warm twelve move 0.9 m on average and close from 0.58 m apart to 0.21 (at pressed they overlap one another in the picture: perhaps 1.2 m2 of the 3 m2 they showed is lost behind another post), and the grey twelve move 0.2 to 0.6 m each (displaced, not hidden: each leaves and covers about 0.2 m2). On a subject of some 60 m2 of frame (the two fields, rail, stand, board): (1.2 + 12 x 0.2 x 2 x 0.3 seen as change) / 60: about 3 %. Open against half is the same grey movement and a warm movement of 0.9 m with no overlap: a little more.

seat_you_take.name: The Seat You Take
seat_you_take.description: A playground for the applied ethics hall: its two miniature seating plans at the size of a body, with the sightlines the hall says a future version could compare. A long table with a head seat and six along its sides; a round table with six seats on a ring. A seat faces another when the other lies within a turn of the neck either side of where the seat points. Tapes at eye height: red between two seats that face each other, a half tape from a seat that faces one that does not face it back. Standing on a seat's disc lights its own tapes and the stand says whom that seat faces and who faces it. NECK changes the turn (30, 60, 90 degrees); ANGLE THE CHAIRS turns the side seats toward the head. Every seat is empty: it counts where a neck can reach, not who is listened to. Axis neck: thirty, sixty, ninety.
seat_you_take.qfep_connection: A plan distributes who can face whom before anyone speaks, and that distribution can be counted; the count changes with the body assumed, and every change gives one seat access by taking it from others.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The furniture does not move. What differs is tape at eye height, 12 mm wide. At sixty the long table shows 11 red pairs and 4 half tapes and the ring 15 red pairs; at ninety the table shows 21 red pairs and the ring the same 15. So ten pairs go from nothing or a half tape to a full red tape: about 10 x 1.6 m x 0.012 m = 0.19 m2 of tape, and two lines of figures on the stand. On a subject of some 50 m2 of frame: about 0.4 %. Thirty against sixty changes more (4 table pairs, 6 ring pairs and the head's four half tapes). The axis is thin in a still by its nature: it draws lines of sight.

two_reports.name: Two Reports
two_reports.description: A robot station for the paraconsistent engineering hall: the small rule table its text asks for. Two report slips (the door is open; the door is closed), two reasoners that are told what the visitor tells them, and seven questions each answers with a lamp: does this follow? The classical reasoner, told both, lights every row, an unrelated lamp among them (on, and off): explosion. The paraconsistent one (the Logic of Paradox: true, false or both) keeps both reports and lights four; the lamp does not follow; and the last row shows the rule it gave up. Two real doors stand beside the slips, one open and one shut: WHERE FROM? gives each report its source, hour and door, and then neither reasoner has a contradiction. Axis told: nothing, one, both.
two_reports.qfep_connection: Two accounts can share a system without one disappearing if the rules of inference stop a contradiction from licensing everything; and provenance may show the accounts never contradicted.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The doors, slips, lamp post and cabinets stand the same at every value. Between nothing and one: one slip card turns yellow (0.9 x 0.62 m = 0.56 m2), one plate tile (0.7 m2 on the floor, seen at a slant: 0.25 m2), four small lamps of 0.018 m2 each and eight lines of lettering change shade. On a subject of some 70 m2 of frame: about 1 m2 / 70 = 1.4 % at most, and under 0.5 % at the hottest twentieth because the changes are scattered. Both against one adds the second card, nine more lamps in red, the lit bulb and the red footer: larger.

four_stations.name: Four Stations, One Walk
four_stations.description: A robot station for the situated computation hall: the next experiment its text proposes, with the visitor's own walk as the subject. A field six metres square with a line up its middle and four stations at its corners. Each sees only what comes within 3.4 m of it and each has its own definition of DANGEROUS (off the line; fast; near me; staying). After a walk from START to END every station says what it saw (how long, what share, how fast, how far off the line, how near), what the word means to it, and its verdict; the walk stays on the floor as a trace coloured by who saw each step. ONE DEFINITION leaves only disagreement from evidence; ONE RECORD leaves only disagreement from definitions; with both they agree. Found with an example walk. Axis sharing: own, one_definition, one_record, both.
four_stations.qfep_connection: A judgement has a subject, an assertion, a criterion and the conditions it was made under; holding the subject fixed, disagreement can be split into what each judge saw and what each judge means.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The field, the stations, the arcs and the example trace are the same at every value. What changes is lettering on four panels (1.9 x 1.56 m each, of which the changing lines cover perhaps a fifth) and two plate tiles. Between one_record and both: one verdict word changes (SW from NOT DANGEROUS to DANGEROUS: about 0.15 m2 and a colour), three 'means' lines change, one tile turns yellow (0.25 m2 seen at a slant), one tally line. On a subject of some 80 m2 of frame: about 0.6 m2: under 1 %, and less at the hottest twentieth. Own against one_definition flips three verdict words: a little more.

marks_and_walls.name: Marks And Walls
marks_and_walls.description: A playground for the collective knowledge hall: a shared record a body can check. A field of five by four cells with walls that cannot be seen on 8 of its 31 inner edges, and on the floor the marks of six earlier sources, each saying 'a wall here' and each keeping who made it and how: felt (a body was stopped) or only told. Some repeat one another, three are wrong, three walls nobody marked. The visitor's body is the test: stopped at a wall, a mark is added or checked; walking through a marked edge strikes its marks, which stay on the floor with who said it and how it was found wrong. SIGN EVERYTHING adds the visitor's told mark to every marked edge. A stand counts marks, sources, felt and told, the edges this body has tested, and how many edges the marks are wrong about. Axis record: found, signed, checked.
marks_and_walls.qfep_connection: A count of contributions is not a measure of what is known; a shared record becomes knowledge where a contribution keeps how it was made and can be checked, corrected and kept as corrected by another body.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: The field, its lines and the stand are the same at every value; the walls are never drawn. What differs is chalk on the floor: found has 11 marks, checked has 14 of which 3 carry a red stroke. Three yellow strokes of 0.9 x 0.06 m and three red strokes are added (about 0.25 m2 with their tags), and four lines of figures change on the stand. Seen at a slant on a subject of some 60 m2 of frame: under 0.5 %. Signed against found adds seven broken yellow strokes: about the same.
